questions.question: Which of the following animals was the emblem of the Chola dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tiger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tiger was the emblem of the Chola dynasty, which was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the history of southern India.
 
• The Chola dynasty used the tiger emblem to symbolize their strength, courage, and dominance over their territory.
 
• The emblem can be found on many of the Chola inscriptions, coins, and temple walls, indicating its importance as a royal insignia.
 
• The tiger emblem not only represented the power of the Chola kings but also their commitment to protecting their kingdom and upholding justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Dynasty**

 
 
• The Chola dynasty was a Tamil dynasty that ruled primarily in southern India until the 13th century.
 
 
• **Tiger Emblem**
 
 
• The tiger symbol was chosen by the Cholas to reflect their royal and warrior status.
 
• The emblem is often depicted in various artistic forms, such as sculptures and carvings, in the temples built by the Chola rulers.
 
• It served as a unifying symbol for the Chola empire, representing the courage and valor of its people.
 
• Historical artifacts like coins and inscriptions bearing the tiger emblem provide insights into the cultural and political landscape of the Chola period.
 
 
 
• **Influence of the Cholas**
 
 
• The Cholas played a pivotal role in the spread of Hinduism and the construction of grand temples, such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
 
• Their naval prowess helped in establishing maritime trade routes with Southeast Asia, contributing to the cultural exchange and economic prosperity of the region.
 
• The Chola administration is noted for its efficient governance, including the development of a systematic revenue collection mechanism.
 
• Their patronage of art and architecture left a lasting legacy that continues to be admired and studied for its grandeur and sophistication.

questions.question: Famous Scholar Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in ________ language.

__
 
• Al-Biruni, a renowned scholar and polymath, wrote the book Kitab-ul-Hind.
 
• Kitab-ul-Hind, also known as "The Book of India," was authored in the Arabic language.
 
• The book is a comprehensive work on Indian culture, philosophy, science, and social customs.
 
• Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind during his time in India in the early 11th century.
 
• This work is considered one of the most important sources of information on medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Al-Biruni:**

 
 
• Born in 973 CE in Khwarezm (present-day Uzbekistan), Al-Biruni was a Persian scholar.
 
• He made significant contributions to various fields, including astronomy, mathematics, and geography.
 
• Al-Biruni traveled extensively, including to India, where he studied its culture and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Kitab-ul-Hind:**
 
 
• This book is a detailed account of Indian life, covering topics such as religion, science, literature, and customs.
 
• It is one of the earliest works by a foreign scholar on Indian society and culture.
 
• The book reflects Al-Biruni's deep respect for Indian knowledge and his objective approach to documenting it.
 
 
 
• **Al-Biruni's Methodology:**
 
 
• Al-Biruni used a scientific and analytical approach in his studies, emphasizing direct observation and evidence-based conclusions.
 
• He learned Sanskrit to understand Indian texts and scriptures better.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Kitab-ul-Hind remains a valuable resource for understanding medieval India from an outsider's perspective.
 
• It provides insights into the interaction between Islamic and Indian civilizations during the early medieval period.

questions.question: The Pandya Kingdom was first mentioned by Megasthenes, who said that their kingdom was famous for pearls. Their capital was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madurai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Madurai was the capital of the ancient Pandya Kingdom, known for its flourishing trade and cultural heritage.
 
• The city is famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple, a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River.
 
• It has been a major settlement for two millennia and is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
 
• Madurai has a rich historical background and has been mentioned in ancient texts and inscriptions, highlighting its significance during the Pandya rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandya Kingdom**

 
 
• The Pandya Kingdom was one of the three ancient Tamil kingdoms, the other two being the Chola and the Chera kingdoms.
 
• The Pandyas were known for their contributions to Tamil literature, art, and architecture.
 
• Their rule is dated back to several centuries BCE, and they were contemporary to other South Indian dynasties like the Cholas and the Cheras.
 
• The Pandyas were great patrons of the Tamil language and literature, which flourished under their rule.
 
 
 
• **Megasthenes**
 
 
• Megasthenes was a Greek historian and diplomat who served as an ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya in India.
 
• His work "Indica" provides an account of the Indian subcontinent during the Maurya Empire, including descriptions of the people, culture, and geography.
 
• Megasthenes' writings are considered valuable historical sources for understanding ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Meenakshi Amman Temple**
 
 
• The Meenakshi Amman Temple is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort, Sundareshwar, a form of Shiva.
 
• The temple complex is a significant symbol of South Indian architecture, featuring tall gopurams (gateway towers) adorned with intricate carvings.
 
• The temple is a major pilgrimage site and attracts millions of visitors and devotees annually.

questions.question: What was the main reason for the defeat of Sirajuddaulah at the Battle of Plassey?

options.text: Britishers cut the food supplies of Sirajuddaulah forces compelling them to surrender.
Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle.
Sirajuddaulah's prime minister misinformed the locations of Britishers.
Britishers knew the secret way to enter Sirajuddaulah's palace.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Battle of Plassey:-

 
 
• When **Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj Ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal.**
 
• The Company was worried about his power and keen on a puppet ruler who would willingly give trade concessions and other privileges.
 
• So it tried, though without success, to help one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's rivals become the nawab.
 
• An infuriated Siraj Ud-Daulah asked the Company to stop meddling in the political affairs of his dominion, stop fortification, and pay the revenues.
 
• After negotiations failed, the **Nawab marched with 30,000 soldiers **to the English factory at Kassimbazar, captured the Company officials, locked the warehouse, disarmed all Englishmen, and blockaded English ships.
 
• Then he marched to Calcutta to establish control over the Company’s fort there.
 
• On hearing the news of the fall of Calcutta, Company officials in Madras sent forces under the command of Robert Clive, reinforced by naval fleets.
 
• In 1757, Robert Clive led the Company’s army against Siraj Ud-Daulah at Plassey.
 
• One of the main reasons for the defeat of the Nawab was that the forces led by Mir Jafar, one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's commanders, never fought the battle.
 
• Robert Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Siraj Ud-Daulah.
 
• The Battle of Plassey became famous because it was the first major victory the Company won in India. 
 
• After the defeat at Plassey, Siraj Ud-Daulah was assassinated and Mir Jafar made the nawab.
 
• The Company was still unwilling to take over the responsibility of the administration.
 
• Its prime objective was the expansion of trade. If this could be done without conquest, through the help of local rulers who were willing to grant privileges, then territories need not be taken over directly.
 
• When Mir Jafar protested, the Company deposed him and installed Mir Qasim in his place.
 
• When Mir Qasim complained, he in turn was defeated in a battle fought at Buxar (1764), driven out of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was reinstalled.

questions.question: At which place was the magnificent temple of Saiva constructed by the great Rashtrakuta King ‘Krishna I’?

__
 
• The magnificent temple of Saiva was constructed by the great Rashtrakuta King 'Krishna I' at **Ellora**.
 
• Ellora is renowned for its monumental caves, which are a mix of Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• The temple constructed by Krishna I is known as the **Kailasa temple**, which is one of the largest rock-cut ancient Hindu temples.
 
• The Kailasa temple is notable for its vertical excavation—carvers started at the top of the rock and excavated downward, which is a unique architectural feat.

• The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the 6th and 10th centuries.
 
• The Rashtrakutas are credited with some of the most significant contributions to art and architecture in India, including the Ellora Caves and the rock-cut temples at Badami.
 
• King Krishna I, who reigned from 756 to 774 CE, was a patron of art and architecture, and his reign saw the construction of the Kailasa temple at Ellora.
 
• The Ellora caves, including the Kailasa temple, are a testament to the religious tolerance during the Rashtrakuta period, as they encompass Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments.
 
• The temple's construction reflects advanced knowledge of engineering and artistry, highlighting the Rashtrakutas' contributions to India's cultural heritage.

questions.question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about ______.

__
 
• **The Ain-i Akbari does not contain** information about Akbar's "**Ancestors**".
 
• The** Ain-i Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama, written by Abul Fazl, one of the Nine Gems (Navratnas) in Akbar's court.**
 
• This document offers a detailed account of **Akbar's reign, including his administration, the state's revenues, and the army.**
 
• However, it does not offer detailed information about his ancestors.

__
 
• The Akbarnama, in its first volume, does discuss Akbar's ancestors, but the **Ain-i Akbari, being the third volume, focuses more on Akbar's own reign and governance, not his lineage.**
 
• Th**e Ain-i Akbari is a five-part book which deals with the court, military establishment, the religions of the empire, the imperial administration, and the social conditions of the empire, among other aspects. It does not delve into the history of Akbar's ancestors.**
 
• The **focus of the Ain-i Akbari is more empirical and administrative, providing intricate details about Akbar's administration, army, and revenue collection.**
 
• **It provides detailed and accurate statistical data about various aspects of Mughal governance.**
 
• The Ain-i Akbari, unlike some other historical documents, isn't a genealogical record or a family history.
 
• **Its primary purpose was to document the empire under Akbar's reign.**

questions.question: Where was the Peshwa sent away with a pension after the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bithur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bithur was the place where Peshwa sent away with a pension after the Third Anglo-Maratha War**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817 – 1818):**

 
 
• After the second Anglo-Maratha war, the Marathas made one last attempt to rebuild their old prestige.
 
• They wanted to retake all their old possessions from the English.
 
• They were also unhappy with the British residents’ interference in their internal matters.
 
• The chief reason for this war was the British conflict with the Pindaris whom the British suspected were being protected by the Marathas.
 
• The Maratha chiefs Peshwa Bajirao II, Malharrao Holkar and Mudhoji II Bhonsle forged a united front against the English.
 
• Daulat Rao Shinde, the fourth major Maratha chief was pressured diplomatically to stay away. But the British victory was swift.
 
• **Results**
 
 
• The Treaty of Gwalior was signed in 1817 between Shinde and the British, even though he had not been involved in the war.
 
• As per this treaty, Shinde gave up Rajasthan to the British.
 
• The Rajas of Rajputana remained the Princely States till 1947 after accepting British sovereignty.
 
• The Treaty of Mandasor was signed between the British and the Holkar chief in 1818. An infant was placed on the throne under British guardianship.
 
• The Peshwa surrendered in 1818. He was dethroned and pensioned off to a small estate in Bithur (near Kanpur). Most parts of his territory became part of the Bombay Presidency.

questions.question: Which Indian dynasty is associated with the creation of highly skilled bronze sculptures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its exceptional craftsmanship in creating bronze sculptures, particularly during the 9th to 13th centuries.
 
• Chola bronze sculptures are characterized by their intricate details and lifelike representation of deities, especially those of Shiva, Parvati, and Nataraja.
 
• The lost-wax casting technique, also known as "cire perdue," was predominantly used by Chola artisans to achieve high precision in their sculptures.
 
• The most iconic representation of Chola bronze art is the Nataraja, depicting Lord Shiva in his cosmic dance form, which symbolizes the cycle of creation and destruction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lost-Wax Casting Technique**:

 
 
• An ancient method of metal casting where a molten metal is poured into a mold created from a wax model.
 
• The wax model is melted and drained away, leaving a hollow form that is filled with molten metal to create the sculpture.
 
 
 
• **Nataraja**:
 
 
• A depiction of the Hindu god Shiva as the cosmic dancer who performs his divine dance to destroy a weary universe and make preparations for the god Brahma to start the process of creation.
 
• The Nataraja iconography is highly symbolic, with the dance representing the rhythmic movement of the universe.
 
 
 
• **Patronage of Arts**:
 
 
• The Chola dynasty was known for its patronage of arts, including temple architecture, painting, and sculpture.
 
• Under their rule, many grand temples were constructed, which served as hubs for artistic activity.
 
 
 
• **Chola Temples**:
 
 
• Notable for their grandeur and intricate architectural designs.
 
• The Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur is one of the most famous examples of Chola architecture.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers built five astronomical observatories at different places in north India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sawai Jaisingh II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sawai Jaisingh II was a notable ruler of the Amber kingdom in the early 18th century.
 
• He built five astronomical observatories, known as Jantar Mantar, located in Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi.
 
• The primary purpose of these observatories was to study the movements of celestial bodies and predict astronomical events.
 
• These observatories are significant examples of Indian scientific heritage and architectural ingenuity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sawai Jaisingh II**

 
 
• He was the ruler of Amber (later Jaipur) from 1699 to 1743.
 
• Jaisingh was a scholar in astronomy, mathematics, and architecture. He was deeply interested in the study of celestial bodies.
 
• His observatories combined elements of Mughal architecture with traditional Indian styles, reflecting his innovative approach.
 
• The observatories were equipped with large instruments made of stone and brass, designed for precise astronomical measurements.
 
 
 
• **Jantar Mantar Observatories**
 
 
• These are collections of architectural astronomical instruments, built in the early 18th century.
 
• The largest of these observatories is located in Jaipur, which also serves as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The instruments at Jantar Mantar were designed to observe and measure the positions of stars, predict eclipses, and ascertain the declinations of celestial bodies.
 
• The observatories are a testament to the advanced scientific knowledge and architectural prowess of that era.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• During the rule of Sawai Jaisingh II, there was significant cultural and scientific exchange between India and other parts of the world.
 
• Jaisingh's patronage of science and architecture led to advancements in various fields, including astronomy, which was crucial for navigation and timekeeping.
 
• The construction of the Jantar Mantar observatories marked a significant period in the history of Indian science and demonstrated the ruler's commitment to knowledge and innovation.

questions.question: Vetti tax is the most frequently mentioned tax in the inscription of Cholas who ruled in Tamil Nadu. This tax was taken in the form of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**forced labour.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vetti Tax:-**

 
 
• **It was a form of forced labor tax levied by the Chola dynasty in southern India. (Hence Option 4 is correct)**
 
• It was the most frequently mentioned tax in Chola inscriptions.
 
• Under the Vetti system, common people were forced to work for the king or their village landlords without any wages.
 
• The Vetti tax was used for a variety of purposes, such as construction and maintenance of public works, such as roads, irrigation systems, and temples.
 
• It was also used to support the military and the royal court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other various taxes imposed by the Chola dynasty:-
 
 
• **Land tax (Kadamai):** This was the most important tax, and was levied on all agricultural land. The rate of tax varied depending on the type of crop and the quality of the land.
 
• **House tax (Manaiya):** This was a tax levied on all houses, regardless of their size or value.
 
• **Market tax (Shulka)**: This was a tax levied on all goods bought and sold in markets.
 
• **Professional tax (Pesha):** This was a tax levied on people who practiced certain professions, such as merchants, artisans, and doctors.

questions.question: ______ wrote a three-volume history of Akbar’s reign, titled ‘Akbar Nama’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abul Fazl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Abul Fazl** was a prominent historian and courtier in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar.
 
• He authored the **three-volume history of Akbar's reign**, known as the **Akbar Nama**.
 
• The **Akbar Nama** is a detailed chronicle of Akbar's life and the history of his reign, written in Persian.
 
• Abul Fazl was also one of the nine jewels (Navaratnas) in Akbar's court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbar Nama**

 
 
• The work is divided into three volumes: the first volume deals with Akbar's ancestors, the second volume records the events of Akbar's reign, and the third volume is the Ain-i-Akbari, which provides detailed information about the administration of the empire.
 
• The **Ain-i-Akbari** is a valuable resource for understanding the administrative system, culture, and society of the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Akbar Nama is considered one of the most important sources of Mughal history.
 
 
 
• **Abul Fazl's Contributions**
 
 
• Besides the Akbar Nama, Abul Fazl also played a crucial role in the administration and cultural development of Akbar's empire.
 
• He was known for his intellectual prowess and was a key advisor to Akbar.
 
• Abul Fazl's writings reflect his deep knowledge of Persian literature, history, and governance.
 
 
 
• **Navaratnas**
 
 
• The Navaratnas were nine extraordinary men in Akbar's court, known for their talents in various fields.
 
• They included notable figures like Birbal, Tansen, and Raja Todar Mal.
 
• The Navaratnas played a significant role in the cultural and intellectual life of the Mughal court.
